DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT RETAINER AGREEMENT

This Retainer Agreement (this "Agreement") is made as of 6 April 2026 between
Kestrel Lane Studio LLC, with its principal office at 118 Fenway Row, Portland,
Maine 04101 ("Studio"), and Northfield Provisions Co., with its principal office
at 27 Alder Street, Concord, New Hampshire 03301 ("Company"). Studio and Company
are each a "Party" and together the "Parties."

1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Retainer Period" means a calendar month during which this Agreement is in
force.

1.2 "Included Hours" means the number of Studio hours per Retainer Period stated
in Section 3.1.

1.3 "Work Request" means a written request from Company for work to be performed
under this Agreement, submitted through the shared project tracker or by email to
Studio's named contact.

1.4 "Work Product" means the designs, documents, code and other material Studio
delivers to Company under this Agreement.

1.5 "Company Materials" means the brand assets, copy, product data and other
material Company supplies to Studio for use in the work.

1.6 "Confidential Information" means non-public information disclosed by one
Party to the other that is marked confidential or that a reasonable person would
understand to be confidential from the circumstances of its disclosure.

1.7 "Business Day" means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or federal holiday
in the United States.

2. SERVICES

2.1 Studio will provide design and front-end development services to Company on
a monthly retainer, in response to Work Requests and in the priority order the
Parties agree at the start of each Retainer Period.

2.2 Studio will perform the work with the degree of skill and care ordinarily
exercised by a competent professional performing work of a similar kind.

2.3 Studio will nominate one person as Company's day-to-day contact and will tell
Company in advance of any change to that nomination.

2.4 Company will nominate one person authorised to submit Work Requests, approve
Work Product and approve changes under Section 4.

2.5 Studio's normal working hours are 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Eastern time on
Business Days, and Studio is under no obligation to perform work outside those
hours.

3. RETAINER, HOURS AND CARRY-OVER

3.1 The retainer is forty (40) Included Hours per Retainer Period.

3.2 Studio will report hours used to Company in writing within five (5) Business
Days after the end of each Retainer Period, with a short description of what the
hours were spent on.

3.3 Up to eight (8) unused Included Hours carry over into the next Retainer
Period. Hours carried over expire if unused in that following period.

3.4 Work in excess of the Included Hours, and any carry-over available, will be
performed only where Company has approved it in advance in writing, and will be
charged at the hourly rate in Section 5.2.

4. CHANGE CONTROL

4.1 Either Party may propose a change to the priorities, the Included Hours or
the scope of any Work Request in progress, by giving the other Party written
notice describing the change.

4.2 A proposed change takes effect when both Parties have confirmed it in
writing, including the effect of the change on hours, fees and delivery dates.

4.3 Where a Work Request in progress turns out to need materially more hours than
estimated, Studio will stop at the estimated figure and tell Company before
continuing, so that Company can decide whether to approve the additional hours or
reduce the request.

4.4 Neither Party is obliged to accept a proposed change, and work continues
under the existing arrangement until a change is confirmed in writing.

5. FEES AND PAYMENT

5.1 The monthly retainer fee is nine thousand six hundred dollars ($9,600),
payable for each Retainer Period.

5.2 Approved work beyond the Included Hours is charged at two hundred and forty
dollars ($240) per hour, billed in fifteen-minute increments.

5.3 Studio will invoice Company on the first Business Day of each Retainer Period
for that period's retainer fee, and in arrears for any approved additional hours
used in the preceding period.

5.4 Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date.

5.5 Interest accrues on any amount that remains unpaid more than thirty (30) days
after its due date, at one percent (1%) per month or the maximum rate permitted
by law, whichever is lower.

5.6 Either Party may dispute an invoice in good faith by giving written notice
within ten (10) Business Days of receiving it, setting out the reason. The
undisputed part of the invoice remains payable on its original due date, and the
Parties will resolve the disputed part promptly.

5.7 Pre-approved third-party costs incurred by Studio on Company's behalf, such
as stock photography licences or font licences, are re-charged at cost with
receipts attached to the relevant invoice.

5.8 Fees are exclusive of sales and use taxes, which are Company's
responsibility where they apply.

6. OWNERSHIP AND LICENCES

6.1 Company retains all right, title and interest in the Company Materials, and
Studio may use them only as needed to perform the work.

6.2 On payment of the invoice covering the Retainer Period in which a piece of
Work Product was delivered, Studio grants Company a perpetual, worldwide,
non-exclusive, fully paid licence to use, modify and distribute that Work Product
for any purpose connected with Company's business.

6.3 Studio retains ownership of its own pre-existing materials, internal tooling,
component libraries and general know-how, none of which is exclusive to Company,
and Section 6.2 does not transfer ownership of any of it.

6.4 Each Party may describe the engagement and display the delivered Work Product
in a portfolio, case study or award submission, once Company has published the
work or given written consent, whichever comes first.

7. CONFIDENTIALITY

7.1 Each Party will keep the other Party's Confidential Information in
confidence, will use it only for the purposes of this Agreement, and will
disclose it only to personnel and advisers who need it for those purposes and who
are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than these.

7.2 The obligations in Section 7.1 do not apply to information that is or becomes
public through no breach of this Agreement, that the receiving Party already held
without a duty of confidence, or that the receiving Party develops independently.

7.3 A Party may disclose Confidential Information where compelled by law or by a
court or regulator, provided that it gives the other Party prompt notice where it
is lawful to do so.

7.4 The obligations in this Section 7 continue for three (3) years after
termination of this Agreement.

8. WARRANTIES

8.1 Each Party warrants that it has the right to enter into this Agreement.

8.2 Studio warrants that the Work Product will be its original work, except for
third-party material identified to Company in writing together with the licence
terms that apply to it.

8.3 Studio warrants that Work Product will conform to the description in the
relevant Work Request for thirty (30) days after delivery, and will correct any
non-conformity reported within that period at no charge.

8.4 Company warrants that it has the right to supply the Company Materials to
Studio for the use contemplated by this Agreement.

9. MUTUAL INDEMNITY

9.1 Each Party will indemnify the other against third-party claims that the
material it supplied under this Agreement infringes that third party's
intellectual property rights, where the claim arises from the indemnifying
Party's own material and not from a modification made by the other Party.

9.2 The indemnifying Party's liability under Section 9.1 is subject to the cap in
Section 10.2.

9.3 A Party seeking indemnity will notify the other promptly, will allow the
indemnifying Party to lead the defence, and will not settle the claim without the
indemnifying Party's written consent.

10. LIABILITY

10.1 Neither Party excludes or limits liability for death or personal injury
caused by its negligence, for fraud, or for any other liability that cannot
lawfully be limited.

10.2 Subject to Section 10.1, each Party's total liability to the other for all
claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement is capped at the total fees
paid and payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months before the event
giving rise to the claim.

10.3 The cap in Section 10.2 applies equally to both Parties, and neither Party
waives any remedy available to it at law or in equity, including the right to
seek specific performance or injunctive relief.

10.4 Each Party remains liable for direct losses caused by its own breach of this
Agreement, and nothing in this Section 10 prevents a Party from recovering unpaid
fees due to it.

11. TERM, TERMINATION AND NOTICE

11.1 This Agreement begins on the date stated above and continues from Retainer
Period to Retainer Period until either Party terminates it.

11.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience, effective at the
end of a Retainer Period, by giving the other Party not less than thirty (30)
days' written notice. The notice period is the same for both Parties.

11.3 Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if
the other Party commits a material breach and does not cure it within fifteen
(15) Business Days of receiving notice describing the breach.

11.4 On termination for any reason, Company will pay Studio for the Retainer
Period in which termination takes effect and for any approved additional hours
already worked, and Studio will deliver to Company all completed and in-progress
Work Product in the form it then exists.

11.5 Termination does not affect any right or remedy that either Party had
accrued before the effective date of termination.

11.6 Sections 6, 7, 9, 10 and 12 survive termination of this Agreement.

12. GENERAL

12.1 Studio is an independent contractor and not an employee, partner or agent of
Company, and nothing in this Agreement creates a joint venture or partnership
between the Parties.

12.2 Each Party is free to work with any other client, customer, supplier or
contractor, including a competitor of the other Party, and nothing in this
Agreement restricts either Party from doing so.

12.3 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and are effective when
delivered by hand, by courier with tracking, or by email to the named contact
with confirmation of receipt.

12.4 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Maine, without regard
to its conflict of laws rules, and the Parties submit to the non-exclusive
jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Cumberland County, Maine.

12.5 Before commencing proceedings, the Parties will each nominate a senior
representative to meet, in person or by video, and attempt in good faith to
resolve the dispute within twenty (20) Business Days of a written request to do
so. This Section 12.5 does not prevent either Party from seeking urgent relief
from a court.

12.6 Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's prior
written consent, except that either Party may assign it in full to a successor in
connection with a merger or a sale of substantially all of its assets.

12.7 Neither Party is liable for a failure or delay in performance caused by an
event beyond its reasonable control, provided that it notifies the other Party
promptly and resumes performance as soon as it is able.

12.8 If any provision of this Agreement is held unenforceable, that provision is
modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable, or if it cannot
be so modified it is severed, and the remaining provisions continue in force.

12.9 This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both
Parties.

12.10 This Agreement is the entire agreement between the Parties on its subject
matter and supersedes all prior discussions, proposals and understandings,
whether written or oral.

12.11 This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic
signature, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one
instrument.

SIGNED for and on behalf of Kestrel Lane Studio LLC

Name: ____________________  Title: ____________________  Date: ____________
